affine_trans_image — 2D geometry op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "affine_trans_image", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: affine_trans_image (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

Sweeping knob a (0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, the other knob at its default):

▸ affine_trans_image: knob a sweep (docs site)

Sweeping knob b (0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, the other knob at its default):

▸ affine_trans_image: knob b sweep (docs site)

On other images (synthetic scene / photo / coins. Top row: inputs, bottom row: their outputs. Knobs at default):

▸ affine_trans_image: other inputs (docs site)

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

A general affine transform combining rotation (`-20 to +20 degrees, determined by a) and shear (determined by b). Applies ndimage.affine_transform relative to the center, filling outside the frame by reflection. Corresponds to HALCON's affine_trans_image` (Apply an arbitrary affine 2D transformation to images) -- HALCON allows passing an arbitrary 2x3/3x3 transform matrix directly, but this is an approximation limited to a two-parameter rotation+shear.
